:::{#def-contour-line}
#### Contour line

For a function $g$ of two real variables $b$ and $c$
and a number $k$,
the **contour line** of $g$ at height $k$
is the set of points where $g$ equals $k$:

$$\cb{(b, c) : g(b, c) = k}$$

On a plot of the surface $z = g(b, c)$,
it is the curve along which the surface has height $k$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-contour-line}
#### Contour lines of a bowl

For $g(b, c) = b^2 + c^2$,
the contour line at height $k = 4$ is $\cb{(b, c) : b^2 + c^2 = 4}$,
the circle of radius $2$ around $(0, 0)$:
for example,

$$
\begin{aligned}
g(2, 0) &= 4 + 0 \\
&= 4
\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}
g(0, -2) &= 0 + 4 \\
&= 4.
\end{aligned}
$$

The contour line at height $k = -1$ is empty,
because $b^2 + c^2 \ge 0$ for all $b$ and $c$.

:::
